## Selective Availability: Two Changes, Seven Years Apart

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the US government stopped using the feature, aiming to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

In September 2007, the government announced that future GPS III satellites would be procured without Selective Availability. This was a procurement choice, not the operational switch made in 2000: it carried the 2000 policy into a future generation.
